domain: Religious Studies / Theology / Philosophy of Science
topic_summary: Analysis of the Genesis 1-2 creation narrative as a contested kernel where different interpretive communities read the same fixed text through incompatible hermeneutical frameworks, generating structurally different constraints on belief, scientific engagement, and communal identity.

key_entities: Young Earth Creationism movement (literalist interpretive authority)
Traditionalist faith communities (beneficiaries of literalist reading)
Modernist faith communities (beneficiaries of harmonizing reading)
key_tensions: Scriptural inerrancy vs empirical evidence primacy
Faith community coherence vs scientific literacy integration

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Genesis 1-2 creation narrative stabilized as canonical scripture with claimed interpretive authority over cosmological origins
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Competing hermeneut frameworks claim legitimacy through either scriptural literalism (sola scriptura tradition) or faith-reason synthesis (Augustinian/Thomistic tradition)

readings.commitment: Genesis describes six literal 24-hour days of creation occurring ~6000-10000 years ago
readings.authority_grounding: Scriptural inerrancy; plain-sense reading as divine revelation immune to empirical correction
readings.expected_structural_delta: Scientific consensus enters victim set; empirical method subordinated to textual authority; high suppression of evolutionary pedagogy

readings.commitment: Genesis describes theological truth through non-literal literary forms compatible with evolutionary cosmology
readings.authority_grounding: Faith-reason synthesis; divine revelation mediated through human literary convention and empirical discovery
readings.expected_structural_delta: Literalist doctrine enters victim set; scientific method coexists with theological claims; textual authority limited to theological domain

readings.commitment: Genesis 1-2 employs Ancient Near Eastern cosmological schema as literary framework without cosmological claims
readings.authority_grounding: Historical-critical method; ancient authorial intent recovered through comparative literature
readings.expected_structural_delta: Both scientific and traditional theological authority displaced; text becomes cultural artifact rather than normative constraint

axiom_contradictions.basis: One reading treats empirical falsifiability as irrelevant to scriptural truth claims (textual authority absolute); the other treats empirical evidence as legitimate correction mechanism (textual authority bounded). No coherent epistemological framework holds both axioms simultaneously.

One reading asserts Genesis makes factual cosmological claims requiring assent; the other denies Genesis intends any cosmological claims. No hermeneutic can simultaneously affirm and deny authorial cosmological intent for the same text.
